component.name: google-firestore
component.title: Google Firestore
component.description: Store, retrieve and query documents in Google Cloud Firestore collections.
component.label: cloud,database

configuration.description: The configuration that each endpoint of this component starts from. The options of the endpoint URI override its values.

databaseId.label: common
databaseId.description: The Firestore database ID. If not specified, the default database '(default)' will be used.

firestoreClient.description: To use a custom com.google.cloud.firestore.Firestore client. When this option is set or autowired, the projectId, databaseId and serviceAccountKey options are not used. The Camel endpoint does not close a client that is set or autowired.

projectId.label: common
projectId.description: The ID of the Google Cloud project. If not set, the Firestore client takes it from the service account key, or from the environment, such as the GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT environment variable.

serviceAccountKey.label: common
serviceAccountKey.description: The service account key file in JSON format that the Firestore client uses as credentials. It is loaded from the classpath by default, or from another location with the prefix file: or http:. If not set, the client uses Application Default Credentials.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

realtimeUpdates.label: consumer
realtimeUpdates.description: Whether the consumer listens for realtime changes of the collection with a snapshot listener. The first snapshot reports every existing document as ADDED, and each poll routes the changes buffered since the previous poll. If false, each poll reads all documents of the collection, so a document is consumed again in every poll.

maxPendingChanges.label: consumer,advanced
maxPendingChanges.description: Maximum number of realtime document changes buffered between two polls. The changes reported by the snapshot listener are buffered until the next poll picks them up, so a collection changing faster than the route consumes it makes that buffer grow. When the buffer is full the oldest buffered change is discarded and a warning is logged. Use 0 for an unbounded buffer. Only used when realtimeUpdates is enabled.

documentId.label: producer
documentId.description: The ID of the document for setDocument, getDocumentById, updateDocument and deleteDocument, which fail without one. For listCollections it is the document whose subcollections are listed, and if not set the root collections are listed. The CamelGoogleFirestoreDocumentId header replaces this option.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

operation.label: producer
operation.description: The operation that the producer performs. If not set, the producer performs setDocument. The CamelGoogleFirestoreOperation header replaces this option.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

healthCheckConsumerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckConsumerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all consumer based health checks from this component

healthCheckProducerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckProducerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all producer based health checks from this component. Notice: Camel has by default disabled all producer based health-checks. You can turn on producer checks globally by setting camel.health.producersEnabled=true.

CamelGoogleFirestoreOperation.label: producer
CamelGoogleFirestoreOperation.description: The operation that the producer performs. It replaces the operation option.

CamelGoogleFirestoreCollectionName.label: producer
CamelGoogleFirestoreCollectionName.description: The name of the collection that the producer uses. It replaces the collection name of the endpoint URI.

CamelGoogleFirestoreDocumentId.label: producer
CamelGoogleFirestoreDocumentId.description: The ID of the document that the producer uses. It replaces the documentId option.

CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryField.label: producer
CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryField.description: The field that queryCollection filters on. The filter is applied only when the CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryOperator and CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryValue headers are also set.

CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryOperator.label: producer
CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryOperator.description: The operator for query filtering: == (or eq), != (or ne), lt (less than), lte (less than or equal), gt (greater than), gte (greater than or equal), array-contains, in, array-contains-any or not-in. The lt, lte, gt and gte operators can also be given as their comparison symbols.

CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryValue.label: producer
CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryValue.description: The value that queryCollection compares the field with. For the in, array-contains-any and not-in operators it must be a java.util.List.

CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryLimit.label: producer
CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryLimit.description: The maximum number of documents that queryCollection returns. If not set, or 0 or less, all matching documents are returned.

CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryOrderBy.label: producer
CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryOrderBy.description: The field that queryCollection orders the documents by.

CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryOrderDirection.label: producer
CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryOrderDirection.description: The direction of the order that CamelGoogleFirestoreQueryOrderBy sets: ASCENDING (the default) or DESCENDING.

CamelGoogleFirestoreResponseDocumentId.description: The ID of the document. The consumer sets it for each document, and the producer for setDocument, createDocument (the generated ID), getDocumentById, updateDocument and deleteDocument.

CamelGoogleFirestoreResponseDocumentPath.description: The path of the document, such as users/alice. The consumer sets it for each document, and the producer for setDocument, createDocument, updateDocument, deleteDocument, and getDocumentById when the document exists.

CamelGoogleFirestoreResponseCreateTime.description: The time the document was created. The consumer sets it for each document, and the producer for getDocumentById when the document exists.

CamelGoogleFirestoreResponseUpdateTime.description: The time the document was last updated. The consumer sets it for each document, and the producer for getDocumentById when the document exists. For setDocument, createDocument, updateDocument and deleteDocument it is the time of the write.

CamelGoogleFirestoreResponseReadTime.description: The time the document was read. The consumer sets it for each document, and the producer for getDocumentById when the document exists.

CamelGoogleFirestoreChangeType.label: consumer
CamelGoogleFirestoreChangeType.description: The type of change reported by the realtime listener: ADDED, MODIFIED or REMOVED. Only set when realtimeUpdates is enabled.

CamelGoogleFirestoreMerge.label: producer
CamelGoogleFirestoreMerge.description: Whether setDocument merges the fields of the body into the existing document instead of replacing the document.

CamelGoogleFirestoreMergeFields.label: producer
CamelGoogleFirestoreMergeFields.description: The names of the fields that setDocument merges when CamelGoogleFirestoreMerge is true. A dotted name such as address.city is the nested field city of address; a com.google.cloud.firestore.FieldPath element is used as it is. The other fields of the body are ignored. If not set, all fields of the body are merged.

consumerOut.description: The fields of the document as a Map, one message per document, with its id, path and times in headers, and with realtimeUpdates the change type. Numbers are Long or Double, a timestamp a com.google.cloud.Timestamp

producerIn.description: The fields to write for setDocument (the default), createDocument and updateDocument: a Map, or JSON object text, which is parsed into a Map. Bytes, a stream, a List, a POJO or no body fail: unmarshal it first. The other operations take their input from options and headers

producerOut.description: The Map of the fields written for setDocument, createDocument and updateDocument (JSON text is now the parsed Map), with the document id and path in headers. By the operation: the fields of the document or null when it does not exist for getDocumentById, true for deleteDocument, a List of Maps with _id and _path entries for queryCollection and listDocuments, and the collection ids for listCollections

collectionName.label: common
collectionName.description: The name of the collection. The consumer reads the documents of this collection, and the CamelGoogleFirestoreCollectionName header replaces it for the producer.

databaseId.label: common
databaseId.description: The Firestore database ID. If not specified, the default database '(default)' will be used.

firestoreClient.description: To use a custom com.google.cloud.firestore.Firestore client. When this option is set or autowired, the projectId, databaseId and serviceAccountKey options are not used. The Camel endpoint does not close a client that is set or autowired.

projectId.label: common
projectId.description: The ID of the Google Cloud project. If not set, the Firestore client takes it from the service account key, or from the environment, such as the GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT environment variable.

serviceAccountKey.label: common
serviceAccountKey.description: The service account key file in JSON format that the Firestore client uses as credentials. It is loaded from the classpath by default, or from another location with the prefix file: or http:. If not set, the client uses Application Default Credentials.

sendEmptyMessageWhenIdle.label: consumer
sendEmptyMessageWhenIdle.description: If the polling consumer did not poll any files, you can enable this option to send an empty message (no body) instead.

By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

pollStrategy.label: consumer,advanced
pollStrategy.description: A pluggable org.apache.camel.PollingConsumerPollingStrategy allowing you to provide your custom implementation to control error handling usually occurred during the poll operation before an Exchange have been created and being routed in Camel.

documentId.label: producer
documentId.description: The ID of the document for setDocument, getDocumentById, updateDocument and deleteDocument, which fail without one. For listCollections it is the document whose subcollections are listed, and if not set the root collections are listed. The CamelGoogleFirestoreDocumentId header replaces this option.

operation.label: producer
operation.description: The operation that the producer performs. If not set, the producer performs setDocument. The CamelGoogleFirestoreOperation header replaces this option.

lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

backoffErrorThreshold.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffErrorThreshold.description: The number of subsequent error polls (failed due some error) that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

backoffIdleThreshold.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffIdleThreshold.description: The number of subsequent idle polls that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

backoffMultiplier.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffMultiplier.description: To let the scheduled polling consumer backoff if there has been a number of subsequent idles/errors in a row. The multiplier is then the number of polls that will be skipped before the next actual attempt is happening again. When this option is in use then backoffIdleThreshold and/or backoffErrorThreshold must also be configured.

greedy.label: consumer,scheduler
greedy.description: If greedy is enabled, then the ScheduledPollConsumer will run immediately again, if the previous run polled 1 or more messages.

healthCheckMaxPollDuration.label: consumer,scheduler
healthCheckMaxPollDuration.description: How long a poll may run before the health check of the consumer reports DOWN. The health check is otherwise based on the polls that are done, so it stays UP while a poll hangs, for example on a read without timeout from a connection that went silent. A poll includes routing the messages it polled, so set this above the longest poll you expect. The poll is not interrupted. The value is in millis (not affected by timeUnit). The default 0 turns this off.

initialDelay.label: consumer,scheduler
initialDelay.description: Milliseconds before the first poll starts.

repeatCount.label: consumer,scheduler
repeatCount.description: Specifies a maximum limit of number of fires. So if you set it to 1, the scheduler will only fire once. If you set it to 5, it will only fire five times. A value of zero or negative means fire forever.

runLoggingLevel.label: consumer,scheduler
runLoggingLevel.description: The consumer logs a start/complete log line when it polls. This option allows you to configure the logging level for that.

scheduledExecutorService.label: consumer,scheduler
scheduledExecutorService.description: Allows for configuring a custom/shared thread pool to use for the consumer. By default each consumer has its own single threaded thread pool.

scheduler.label: consumer,scheduler
scheduler.description: To use a cron scheduler from either camel-spring or camel-quartz component. Use value spring or quartz for built in scheduler

schedulerProperties.label: consumer,scheduler
schedulerProperties.description: To configure additional properties when using a custom scheduler or any of the Quartz, Spring based scheduler. This is a multi-value option with prefix: scheduler.

startScheduler.label: consumer,scheduler
startScheduler.description: Whether the scheduler should be auto started.

timeUnit.label: consumer,scheduler
timeUnit.description: Time unit for initialDelay and delay options.

useFixedDelay.label: consumer,scheduler
useFixedDelay.description: Controls if fixed delay or fixed rate is used. See ScheduledExecutorService in JDK for details.
